newsitem.title: USA: Average vehicle price hit record $21,750 in 1996 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Average vehicle price hit record $21,750 in 1996 - dealers.

text.p: Consumers on average paid a record $21,750 for a typical new vehicle in 1996, $1,300 more than the previous year, the National Automobile Dealers Association said in a report distributed to its members Friday.

The 6.4 percent increase over the 1995 average selling price of $20,450 was due almost entirely to consumers' continuing shift from passenger cars to more expensive sport utility vehicles, said NADA chief economist Thomas Webb.

"Sport utilities and a shift to the luxury end of the market were the biggest reasons for the increase," Webb said. "If you were to look at pricing on any individual vehicle, you would see flat to negative changes in price."

The NADA report also said the average used-vehicle transaction price reached a record $11,600 in 1996, up from $11,050 in 1995. Webb said the increase was due partly to the continued influx of low-mileage, two-year-old cars onto dealers lots from leases.

Franchised dealerships sold more used vehicles than new for the eighth consecutive year in 1996 as used vehicle sales rose to a record 19.2 million from 18.5 million in 1995. Sales of new vehicles rose to 15.1 million units from 14.8 million.
Other findings of the report, distributed to the trade group's 19,500 member dealerships:

-- The new-vehicle department contributed 58 percent of total dealership sales dollars, compared to 67 percent 10 years ago. The used-vehicle department contributed 30 percent, the service and parts department 12.4 percent.

-- Service and parts sales increased 8 percent, double the rate of growth in 1995. Dealerships completed 221 million repair orders in 1996, for total sales of $61 billion. More than half of all dealerships now offer evening or weekend hours in the service department.

-- Dealerships increased advertising outlays by 10 percent in 1996, to a record $5.1 billion, from $4.6 billion in 1995. The lion's share of the increase went to used-vehicle advertising, which accounted for 33 percent of all advertising expenditures last year.
-- Dealers added 34,700 employees to their payrolls in 1996, bringing total dealership employment to over 1 million people and total payroll to $35 billion.
